parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { study_id: 'study_test_05', building_id: 'bldg_001', zone_ids: ['north_entrance_lobby'], behavior_targets: [{ behavior_name: 'Utilization Rate', behavior_description: 'Percentage of capacity being used over time', behavior_units: 'percentage' }], setup_instructions: 'Monitor the main turnstile zone for occupant flow behaviors.', last_etag_seen: null, review_mode: false, debug_mode: true, camera_id: 'camera_1' } }];

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ success: true, study_id: $json.body.study_id, message: 'Study monitoring started' }) }}

parameters.jsonBody:
={{ JSON.stringify({ model: 'gpt-4.1', input: [{ role: 'system', content: [{ type: 'input_text', text: 'You are a building behavior monitoring agent. Analyze the image and return ONLY valid JSON with these exact keys:
- detected_behaviors: array of objects, each with { name, value, unit }
- occupant_count: integer or null
- notes: string

IMPORTANT: You MUST return one entry in detected_behaviors for EVERY behavior listed in the input, even if the value is 0. Never return an empty detected_behaviors array.

PRIVACY: When describing individuals in the notes field, focus on behavioral and spatial observations only. You may describe posture (seated, standing, leaning), position in the space (left, center, right), orientation (facing camera, facing away), and functional accessories relevant to behavior (headphones suggest solo focus, shared screen suggests collaboration). Do NOT describe clothing colors, clothing items, hair, or any other visual characteristic that could identify a specific person. Use anonymous labels (P1, P2, etc.) and keep descriptions behaviorally relevant.

TEMPORAL CONTEXT: You will receive two optional fields:
- study_context: a statistical summary of all detections so far (mean, min, max, trend per behavior)
- recent_detections: the last 3 raw detections with timestamps, values and notes

CRITICAL: The current image is ALWAYS the primary source of truth. Use past context only to identify trends and changes — never let it override what you can clearly see in the image right now. If the current image contradicts recent detections, trust the image. Only reference past context in your notes when it adds meaningful insight.' }] }, { role: 'user', content: [{ type: 'input_text', text: 'Study: ' + $json.study_id + '
Camera: ' + ($json.camera_id || 'camera_1') + '
Zone: ' + ($json.zone_id || 'unknown') + '
Behaviors:
' + ($json.behavior_targets || []).map(b => '- ' + b.behavior_name + ' (' + (b.behavior_units || 'value') + ')' + (b.behavior_description ? ' — ' + b.behavior_description : '') + (b.behavior_rubric ? '
  Rubric: ' + b.behavior_rubric : '')).join('
') + ($json.study_context ? '

Study context (all detections so far):
' + JSON.stringify($json.study_context, null, 2) : '') + ($json.recent_detections && $json.recent_detections.length > 0 ? '

Last ' + $json.recent_detections.length + ' detections:
' + JSON.stringify($json.recent_detections, null, 2) : '') }, { type: 'input_image', image_url: $json.image_data_url }] }], max_output_tokens: 1500 }) }}

parameters.jsCode: return [{ json: { ...$json, snapshot_uploaded: false, snapshot_path: null } }];
